resolutions.gate_case: NONE — and this is stated rather than skipped. A check asserting "every 'N held-out' reads 7" would go red on roughly ten legitimately historical measurement records (ADR-020:146/:275, ADR-026:167/:172, ADR-029:175, ADR-030:46, ADR-031:16, ADR-032:35/:299/:360, ADR-033:42 all correctly say 5 for the date they measured). Separating a present-tense claim about the current corpus from a dated record of a past one is not mechanizable from free prose, and a check that fires on ten true sentences to catch four false ones is worse than the staleness. The finding's own evidence says the same: "No eval case could have gone red on this."

It now lists only items 2, 3, 5, 7A, 9B and 15, with the reason restated accurately (3 is Pages 102-105 nested inside item 8's 56-108; 15 is 56-108 plus 110-115), and says outright that 9A is NOT in that list, that its exclusion has no evidentiary reason, and that it is as floorable from the index alone as 1A's 37-51 is.
resolutions.floor_half: REJECTED as a repair, and the substance is conceded — the hole is real and is now stated inside the case itself as declination (f) and logged as a Debt row (Origin: D6 / PR #52 R7). The reason is process, not evidence. The H4 baseline is already committed against this case's check list; adding a check now either falsifies that committed report — the README H4 entry states that the five red checks are the four floors and the one anchor — or forces a re-run. And a re-run chosen after I had read the outcome, adding an assertion I picked knowing 9A came back a 43-char stub at 0.95, is precisely the retrofit the freeze exists to prevent. The burn rule names 'a threshold choice' as influence; the `gs-2002` and `axp-2008` precedents both burned on weaker influence than deriving a new threshold with the outcome in hand. Closing this hole that way would cost the exam itself, which is the whole deliverable of D6. It is carried at authoring by the next held-out expansion, where it costs nothing.
resolutions.gate_case: NONE for either half. The prose half is a factual claim about a filing's index inside free prose; the floor half is deliberately not implemented.
